doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27

title: Teaching Chink Martin tuba, and La Rocca sitting in
summary: Laine tells how he put Chink Martin on tuba for a Wild West show when Cascaro fell sick, and how Nick La Rocca began sitting in with his band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Let me tell you a little story about the Chinamen. I had them on bass pedal and had them on guitar all the time, you know. And it seemed like I needed more tuba players. I only had two at the time, you understand? Then I got Lawyer Cannon, May Street, and I had to get five tuba players anyway. So, here comes young Buffalo Bill, a fellow by the name O'Brien, for the Wild West Show. Well, they found out about me, you understand? They come down to shame me. And I had Cascaro on tuba. Cascaro took Deathly Sick. He died shortly after that, too. I believe it was Poison. So, here I had this job. And that show was in the lot on Espinade between the river and Decatur, on the downtown side of the street. Great big tent show, Wild West Show. Cascaro sent my word, impossible. Couldn't play. Jesus, I said, what am I going to do now? Had all the other players engaged, playing their jobs. What did I do? I go to Cascaro's house and get these tuba. Called the gentleman, you come on out here. Now get in this band. Here, play this. The gentleman said, what the hell do I know about that? The kids, you know, I don't know nothing about that. Shove that in your face and play it.

All right, he said. If you say so, it's all right. We stood by number nine, Jane Jane House, on Decatur and Espinade. I lined them all around the circle. Said to the Chinaman, I said, whenever you can catch time, the Chinaman, that you can fill up a note, put it in there. This baritone, I said, hold up as much as possible for you. All right. Put the tuba in the Chinaman's hand. Every night we played for two weeks. Every night for two weeks. Chinaman on the tube. Start to put them in parades. Start to moat around. Said to that, that Chinaman played a tuba. I went to Cascro, the old lady, his mother, and I bought the tuba. Eight dollars. Eight dollars. Eight dollars. Eight dollars. I'll give it to the Charmin. Ever since that, the chick was playing. No more bass, middle guitar. Tuba. You sure picked a good one, too. Yeah. Now, the same way you take La Rocca. Nick, Nick come down a couple of times in my rehearsal, you know. And, uh, he'd sit around listening, you know, one thing or another. And, uh, bring down his cornet and he'd listen around there, you know. And the first thing you know, I got through that much work, Johnny, that I put him in the band anyhow to fill out. To fill out. Go along, go along. Even over at Elmire Pleasure Ground. Over at, uh, at, uh, Algier Park. All around there, I had every Saturday and Sunday. Cramer's lot. Three or four of them places over there. Had them on Saturdays and Sundays. La Rocca used to come and sit on Saturdays and Sunday.
